source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Induce labor contractions in the antepartum period, which does not describe why oxytocin is actually being given at this particular postpartum moment","B":"Promote uterine contraction to prevent postpartum hemorrhage, rather than induce labor as the family member is currently assuming","C":"Relieve postpartum pain at the delivery site, which is not the actual purpose of oxytocin in this particular clinical context","D":"Prevent the onset of postpartum depression, which is not an effect or purpose associated with this particular medication"}}
source_row.rationale: After delivery of the placenta, oxytocin is commonly administered to promote firm uterine contraction (uterine tone), which helps compress the blood vessels at the placental implantation site, reducing the risk of postpartum hemorrhage — a distinct indication from its use in labor induction/augmentation.
source_row.source_detail: Oxytocin Use for Postpartum Hemorrhage Prevention
source_row.stem: A nurse anticipates administering oxytocin to a client immediately after delivery of the placenta, and a family member assumes this medication is being given to help induce further labor contractions. The purpose of this medication in this particular context is instead to:
